history.content: Immutable Object Storage is a feature provided by IBM Cloud Object Storage that allows users to configure buckets with a policy to prevent objects from being modified or deleted for a defined period of time. This retention period can be specified on a per-object basis or objects can inherit a default retention period set on the bucket. It is also possible to set open-ended and permanent retention periods. This feature can help users meet the rules set forth by various regulations regarding record retention, such as SEC Rule 17a-4(f), FINRA Rule 4511(c), and CFTC Rule 1.31(c)-(d). However, it is the client's responsibility to ensure that the feature capabilities can be used to satisfy and comply with these rules. Note that Immutable Object Storage meets the rules set forth by the SEC governing record retention, and IBM Cloud administrators are unable to bypass these restrictions. Once permanent retention is enabled, it cannot be reversed and objects uploaded with a permanent retention period cannot be deleted. Users are responsible for ensuring that their IBM Cloud Account is kept in good standing per IBM Cloud policies and guidelines for as long as the data is subject to a retention policy.
Why are there regulations set regarding records retention? Who decides that?

Regulations regarding records retention are set to ensure that important records of organizations are kept for a certain period of time, which can be useful for various purposes such as auditing, compliance, and legal obligations. These regulations are generally decided by governmental bodies or regulatory authorities relevant to the specific industry or field. For instance, in the financial industry, regulations like SEC Rule 17a-4(f), FINRA Rule 4511(c), and CFTC Rule 1.31(c)-(d) govern electronic records storage and retention. Organizations retain audit records until it is determined that they are no longer needed for administrative, legal, audit, or other operational purposes. This includes, for example, retention and availability of audit records relative to Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) requests, subpoenas, and law enforcement actions. Organizations develop standard categories of audit records relative to such types of actions and standard response processes for each type of action. The National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) General Records Schedules provide federal policy on record retention. It is the client's responsibility to ensure that their use of Immutable Object Storage complies with these regulations.
Who sets the regulations for the health and insurance industries?

So Immutable Object Storage is an advantage if disaster recovery capability is needed?

Yes, Immutable Object Storage can be beneficial in a disaster recovery scenario. It provides a mechanism for preserving data integrity and preventing accidental or malicious deletion or modification of objects for a defined period.  If you are using Cloud Object Storage for backup, at minimum, use separate buckets for backing up different workload accounts. Also, use separate backup credentials for each bucket where service to service policies are not possible. Use Cloud Object Storage versioning or immutable buckets for maximum security.However, it's important to note that using Immutable Object Storage is just one aspect of a comprehensive disaster recovery strategy. Other factors, such as data backup, system redundancy, and failover procedures, should also be considered to ensure a robust disaster recovery capability.  IBM follows best practices for disaster recovery.

Prerequisites 



* IBM Cloud account and an instance of IBM Cloud® Object Storage
* A Linux or macOS environment
* Credentials (either an [IAM API key](https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/cloud-object-storage/iam?topic=cloud-object-storage-iam-overview) or [HMAC credentials](https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/cloud-object-storage?topic=cloud-object-storage-uhc-hmac-credentials-main))







 Installation 

On Debian or Ubuntu:

sudo apt-get install automake autotools-dev fuse g++ git libcurl4-openssl-dev libfuse-dev libssl-dev libxml2-dev make pkg-config



The official s3fs documentation suggests using libcurl4-gnutls-dev instead of libcurl4-openssl-dev. Either work, but the OpenSSL version may result in better performance.

For macOS, you will need to build s3fs from source:

Ensure you have the following packages installed (all are available via [Homebrew](https://brew.sh)):



* macfuse
* automake
* gcc

Replications that use IAM API keys can be updated to use a new API key directly, without delaying the changes that are replicating.



* What is the difference between IBM Cloudant legacy and IAM access controls?



 IBM Cloud IAM 



* Centrally managed access management across IBM Cloud.
* Allows a user or service to access many different resources by using the same set of credentials (for example, same username and password or IAM API key).
* IAM API keys can be granted access to account management functions, like creating new databases.







 IBM Cloudant legacy 



* Unique to IBM Cloudant.
* Access to each service instance requires its own set of credentials.
* Uses HTTP basic authentication with credentials that aren't bound to an individual user or service.





* Why is the Use only IAM mode preferred?

After a root key has been created, neither a user nor IBM can see its key material.
* What is a data encryption key (DEK)?

A DEK is a key used by services like IBM Cloud Object Storage service to perform IBM-managed AES256 encryption of the data stored in the cloud object storage. The DEK keys are randomly generated and stored securely with the cloud object storage service near the resources they encrypt. The DEK is used for default encryption in all cases regardless of whether the customer wants to manage the encryption keys or not. The ICOS DEK is not managed by clients nor do they need to rotate it. For cases where clients do want to manage the encryption, they indirectly control the DEK by wrapping the DEK with their own "root key" stored in their Key Protect instance. A root key can be generated or imported, and managed by you in your Key Protect instance (for example, by rotating keys).
